raw.setup_notes: 125B MoE hybrid on a single 24GB card: 6892 experts (~13.4 GB) in VRAM, rest in RAM, lookup table on NVMe. VRAM permanently occupied 23471/24564 MiB (processes /strata + /strata-vision). Speculative decoding MTP=4 + lookup=3, pcie_frac 0.35, image input enabled, one request at a time. WSL2 is not an officially documented path: RAM must be allocated via .wslconfig (96 GB here) or the engine can't load the 35-55 GB of experts. 4x32GB double-rank DDR4 holding 3600 CL18 (unusual on Ryzen 5000 - most boards drop to 3200 with this many ranks), so the RAM-resident experts get ~57 GB/s of dual-channel bandwidth.

submissions.notes: 125B MoE hybrid on a single 24GB card: 6892 experts (~13.4 GB) in VRAM, rest in RAM, lookup table on NVMe. VRAM permanently occupied 23471/24564 MiB (processes /strata + /strata-vision). Speculative decoding MTP=4 + lookup=3, pcie_frac 0.35, image input enabled, one request at a time. WSL2 is not an officially documented path: RAM must be allocated via .wslconfig (96 GB here) or the engine can't load the 35-55 GB of experts. 4x32GB double-rank DDR4 holding 3600 CL18 (unusual on Ryzen 5000 - most boards drop to 3200 with this many ranks), so the RAM-resident experts get ~57 GB/s of dual-channel bandwidth. | dedicated Qwen3.8-Flash-Next engine, OpenAI/Anthropic API Hi, Please note that big parts of this post have been written with the help of the hereafter described model using OpenWork harness as I was afraid to miss relevant infos Strata on a 4090 + 128 GB, under WSL2 — agentic coding Direct answer to @lhl (post #25): yes, Strata changes the “small GPU” equation. A Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B in IQ3_S runs on a single 4090 here, at ~108 tok/s decode in real agent use. Beyond raw speed, what sold me is the prompt cache: ~90% hit rate, so agent follow-ups on ~50k-token contexts resume in 0.3-0.8 s instead of re-prefilling. One note for anyone eyeing WSL2: the docs target native Windows or native Linux. Under WSL2 you must allocate RAM explicitly (.wslconfig, 96 GB here - WSL2 defaults to 50% of host), otherwise the engine doesn’t have enough RAM to load the 35-55 GB of experts. I came from llama.cpp (Qwen3.8-27B-UD-IQ4_X@256k, KV q4_0), where I was already doing very good agentic coding with Claude Code or Copilot CLI (both via VSCode terminal). No formal comparison, but Strata at IQ3_S/131k doesn’t make me miss the 27B at 256k - I do miss some context depth, and I’m planning to test 256k under Strata. On the tier brackets: with hybrid offload engines (Strata), the VRAM tier alone no longer describes what actually fits - this 125B IQ3_S run is RAM+SSD-bound, not VRAM-bound. A RAM column or an “hybrid/offload” flag would be more honest than a VRAM bracket. Cheers !
